knowledge:
- key_parameters:
    - dataset = The input data frame containing phenotypic data to be analyzed.
    - testGenotype = Mandatory character string defining the test genotype (e.g., "experimental").
    - refGenotype = Mandatory character string defining the reference genotype (e.g., "control").
    - dataset.colname.genotype = Column name in the dataset representing genotype.
    - dataset.colname.batch = Column name in the dataset representing batch or date of experiment.
    - dataset.colname.sex = Column name in the dataset representing sex.
    - dataset.colname.weight = Column name in the dataset representing body weight.
    - dataset.colname.lifestage = Column name in the dataset representing lifestage.
    - debug = Logical flag to enable (TRUE) or disable (FALSE) step-by-step progress messages.
    - method = Character string defining the statistical framework: "MM" (Linear Mixed Model), "FE" (Fisher's Exact Test), or "RR" (Reference Range Plus).
    - MM_fixed = Formula defining the fixed effects for the Linear Mixed Model.
    - MM_random = Formula defining the random effects for the Linear Mixed Model (default is ~1 | Batch).
    - FE_formula = Formula defining the model for Fisher's Exact Test.
    - RR_formula = Formula defining the model for the Reference Range Plus framework.
    - RRrefLevel = Reference level for the Reference Range Plus framework (default is "control").
    - RR_prop = Proportion of normal variation in the Reference Range Plus framework (default is 0.95).
    - MM_checks = Vector of four logical values to activate pre-checks on model terms, single-level factors, zero-variation continuous terms, and interaction terms.
    - FERR_FullComparisions = Vector of two logical flags for RR or FE frameworks to test all factor combinations and response level comparisons.
    - MMFERR_conf.level = Confidence level for estimates across all frameworks (default is 0.95).
    - JSON = Logical flag in OpenStatsReport to output results in JSON format.
- alternatives:
    - PhenStat: OpenStats supports PhenList objects from the Bioconductor PhenStat package as direct inputs to the OpenStatsAnalysis function.
- when_to_use:
    - Use the Linear Mixed Model framework (method = "MM") for continuous phenotypic data where baseline values are normally distributed and batch is a source of variation.
    - Use the Reference Range Plus framework (method = "RR") for continuous data when the linear mixed model fails or when there is a large number of controls (more than 60 records) to identify normal variation.
    - Use Fisher's Exact Test (method = "FE") for categorical phenotypic data to compare proportions and calculate percentage changes.
- pitfalls:
    - The statistical analysis requires exactly two genotype groups for comparison (reference vs. test); records with other genotype values are filtered out if dataset.clean is TRUE.
    - Activating interaction checks (the fourth element of MM_checks) can significantly increase computation time if the formula contains many factors.
    - The normality test result/p-value in the diagnostic plots should be interpreted with caution.
    - If the response variable is not categorical, the FE framework will report that it is not categorical and skip the analysis.

workflows.name: linear_mixed_model_workflow
workflows.intent: Perform genotype-to-phenotype association analysis on continuous data using a Linear Mixed Model (LMM) framework, including split-effect estimation, reporting, and plotting.
input: test_continuous.csv (CSV file containing continuous phenotypic measurements, genotype, sex, batch, and weight columns)
workflows.stages:
1. Preprocess continuous data and create an OpenStatsList object using OpenStatsList.
2. Run the Linear Mixed Model analysis using OpenStatsAnalysis with method = "MM".
3. Estimate split effects with respect to variables (e.g., Sex) using OpenStatsComplementarySplit.
4. Generate a summary table of the analysis using summary.
5. Export detailed reports in JSON format using OpenStatsReport.
6. Plot model diagnostics using plot.
workflows.code:
fileCon <- system.file("extdata", "test_continuous.csv",
  package = "OpenStats"
)
test_Cont <- OpenStatsList(
  dataset = read.csv(fileCon),
  testGenotype = "experimental",
  refGenotype = "control",
  dataset.colname.genotype = "biological_sample_group",
  dataset.colname.batch = "date_of_experiment",
  dataset.colname.lifestage = NULL,
  dataset.colname.weight = "weight",
  dataset.colname.sex = "sex",
  debug = FALSE
)
MM_result <- OpenStatsAnalysis(
  OpenStatsList = test_Cont,
  method = "MM",
  MM_fixed = data_point ~ Genotype + Weight,
  debug = FALSE
)
Spliteffect <- OpenStatsComplementarySplit(
  object = MM_result,
  variables = "Sex"
)
summary(MM_result)
OpenStatsReport(
  object = MM_result,
  JSON = TRUE,
  RemoveNullKeys = TRUE,
  pretty = TRUE
)
plot(MM_result, col = 2)

workflows.name: reference_range_plus_workflow
workflows.intent: Perform genotype-to-phenotype association analysis on continuous data using the Reference Range Plus framework when LMM is not suitable or control sample size is large.
input: test_continuous.csv (CSV file containing continuous phenotypic measurements, genotype, and sex columns)
workflows.stages:
1. Preprocess continuous data and create an OpenStatsList object using OpenStatsList.
2. Run the Reference Range Plus analysis using OpenStatsAnalysis with method = "RR".
workflows.code:
fileCon <- system.file("extdata", "test_continuous.csv",
  package = "OpenStats"
)
test_Cont <- OpenStatsList(
  dataset = read.csv(fileCon),
  testGenotype = "experimental",
  refGenotype = "control",
  dataset.colname.genotype = "biological_sample_group",
  dataset.colname.batch = "date_of_experiment",
  dataset.colname.lifestage = NULL,
  dataset.colname.weight = "weight",
  dataset.colname.sex = "sex",
  debug = FALSE
)
RR_result <- OpenStatsAnalysis(
  OpenStatsList = test_Cont,
  method = "RR",
  RR_formula = data_point ~ Genotype + Sex
)

workflows.name: fishers_exact_test_workflow
workflows.intent: Perform genotype-to-phenotype association analysis on categorical data using Fisher's Exact Test.
input: test_categorical.csv (CSV file containing categorical phenotypic measurements, genotype, and sex columns)
workflows.stages:
1. Preprocess categorical data and create an OpenStatsList object using OpenStatsList.
2. Run Fisher's Exact Test analysis using OpenStatsAnalysis with method = "FE".
workflows.code:
fileCat <- system.file("extdata", "test_categorical.csv",
  package = "OpenStats"
)
test_Cat <- OpenStatsList(
  dataset = read.csv(fileCat, na.strings = "-"),
  testGenotype = "Aff3/Aff3",
  refGenotype = "+/+",
  dataset.colname.genotype = "Genotype",
  dataset.colname.batch = "Assay.Date",
  dataset.colname.lifestage = NULL,
  dataset.colname.weight = "Weight",
  dataset.colname.sex = "Sex",
  debug = FALSE
)
FE_result <- OpenStatsAnalysis(
  OpenStatsList = test_Cat,
  method = "FE",
  FE_formula = Thoracic.Processes ~ Genotype + Sex
)
